name: beta-Si3N4, 295 K synchrotron refinement
citation: D. du Boulay, N. Ishizawa, T. Atake, V. Streltsov, K. Furuya and F. Munakata (2004). Synchrotron X-ray and ab initio studies of beta-Si3N4. Acta Crystallographica B 60, 388-405.
conditions_evidence: CIF cell and diffraction temperature tags both give 295 K. Primary article section 2 and Tables 1-2 identify this as crystal 1 measured by single-crystal synchrotron XRD. Measurement pressure not specified.
method: Experimental single-crystal synchrotron diffraction at Photon Factory BL14A, Rigaku four-circle; deposited wavelength 0.75022 A. Selected P63/m independent-atom refinement, not the separate ab-initio calculation.
synthesis_conditions_note: Primary article section 2, printed p.390: pure silicon melt in a silicon nitride crucible; recovered single-crystal fragments. The 1900 K synthesis temperature is not the 295 K measurement temperature.
selection: Selected measured beta nitride alternative after SiC source screening. Source inspection only; no native FEFF or sample fit performed.
notes: Raw CIF _cell_formula_units_Z=1.5 conflicts with the symmetry-expanded Si6N8 composition (Z=2); original bytes retained. Potentials must use actual expanded composition, not the erroneous Z metadata.
This is beta-Si3N4 with Si-N scattering; it is not a SiC or Si-C reference.
Primary Table 6, printed p.394, reports the 295 K P63/m Si-N distances 1.72976(10), 1.7357(3), and 1.73567(16) twice, agreeing with regenerated geometry within deposited precision.
The primary study found no compelling support for lower-symmetry P63. The deposited P63 alternatives and lower-temperature measurements are not additional absorbers in this pilot.
All raw occupancies are 1.00000; strict and generator cells both contain Si6N8, 14 atoms, with one Si orbit. No atoms or occupations were edited.
